title: DECODE & SOLVE (ROLE PLAY)
rules:
1. Rules and Regulations:
    • Each team must consist of exactly 3 participants. No substitutions or additions will be allowed after the event begins.
    • The competition consists of two rounds: Round 1: Decode and Round 2: Solve. Final ranking will be based on the total score obtained in Round 1 and Round 2, out of 50 marks.
    • The clues may be based on, but are not limited to: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing, Robotics, Other Emerging Technologies.
  2. Round 1 - Decode:
    • Teams must analyze the provided clues and correctly identify the technology, concept, or problem being described.
    • Teams will have 10 minutes to discuss and submit a single answer sheet containing the identified technology or concept.
    • Teams may submit their answer before the allotted time expires. Once submitted, no changes or resubmissions will be permitted.
    • During this round, the use of mobile phones, smartwatches, laptops, tablets, internet access, AI tools, or any other electronic device is strictly prohibited.
    • Only teams that correctly identify the intended technology/concept in Round 1 will proceed to Round 2. The judges' interpretation of the clues and their scoring decisions shall be final.
  3. Round 2 - Solve:
    • Teams will design a solution (system, app, workflow, architecture, or prototype concept) to a real-world problem.
    • Teams will have 10 minutes to prepare, using only the chart paper/materials provided. Output may be an architecture diagram, flowchart, algorithm, pseudocode, interface sketch, or verbal proposal.
    • Round 2 presentation time shall be a maximum of 7 minutes, followed by up to 3 minutes for judges' questions. The judges may stop a team when the allotted presentation time expires.
    • The proposed solution must clearly explain: How the technology works, How it solves the given problem, Why the solution is practical and technically feasible.
    • Teams will be judged on technical understanding, reasoning, creativity, and feasibility.
    • All 3 members must present and may take any question. Judges may also ask for an individual response.
  4. General Rules:
    • Leaving the competition area mid-round needs organizer permission.
    • Tie-break: if two or more teams are tied on total score, judges will ask the tied teams extra questions in a tie-breaker round to decide the final rank.
